scenario: AITA for not staying home and taking care of my sick wife all weekend? | On Thursday evening my wife started feeling unwell. I encouraged her to go to bed and told her I could handle the kids evening stuff by myself (3 kids, ages 9, 11, and 13). I checked on her after the kids were in bed at 9 and she was fevered- I asked if she wanted any medicine, made sure she had some water, and rubbed her back for a few minutes. I slept in the spare room but got up twice to check on her. The next morning I got the kids ready and off to school, went to a meeting and came home at 10 to take her to the doctor. I worked from home until our cleaning lady came around 1 and asked her to keep an eye on my wife and went back into the office for a couple meetings, picked up the kids and was home around 4. Her fever broke shortly after I got home at 4 and I helped her shower. Our oldest had a school dance and I got some movies and set the youngest 2 up in the den for the evening with pizza and some games so they'd be quiet. I checked on my wife periodically and after the oldest got home me and the 3 kids camped out in the den. On Saturday morning, the kids were restless so I took them out for the day bc I didn't want them to be around the house being loud. I checked on my wife and she was sleeping- I refilled her water and left her a note. Throughout the day I called and sent her messages and my mom took her over some homemade soup and checked on her. We were gone the majority of the day but the kids came home worn out and we crashed in the den again. I checked on my wife as soon as we got home and she was looking better. Sunday morning, the kids and I woke up early, did some yardwork then went to the store to do the weekly grocery shopping. When we got home my wife was up and about and still weak but feeling better. However, she was being really short with me and was in a bad mood. I thought it was just bc she didn't feel well but after a few hours of her making snide comments I asked her if something was wrong and she exploded on me that her family abandoned her while she was sick. She went off about how she always takes care of us when we're sick but we avoided her like the plague and didn't stay home and I made the cleaning lady and my mom take care of her instead of doing it myself. I tried to explain that I didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and I didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest and I checked on her multiple times. She said I should've sent the kids to my parents or something and stayed home and she can't believe I didn't sleep with her for 3 days. I starting getting angry and told her that I did what I thought was best and she sounded ungrateful bc it wasn't exactly what she would've done. She then called me an asshole. We went to bed angry and didn't really speak this morning. I keep stewing over this bc I don't think that I'm an asshole but maybe I am?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user provided a detailed situation where a husband didn't stay home to take care of his sick wife all weekend. Instead, he handled the kids, went to meetings, worked from home, and even took the kids out for the day. His wife got upset, feeling abandoned, and they had a big argument.

First, I need to understand the context. The husband's wife was sick with a fever, and he took care of the kids, made sure she had medicine and water, checked on her multiple times, and even had help from their cleaning lady and his mom. He worked from home, managed meetings, and tried to keep the kids quiet so she could rest. On the other hand, the wife felt neglected because he wasn't there all the time, and she was upset that he didn't stay home to take care of her exclusively.

I think the key points here are responsibility, care, and communication. The husband did take some actions to care for his wife—he checked on her, made sure she had what she needed, and even had others help out. But the wife felt that he wasn't present enough, which led to her frustration and anger.

I wonder if the husband's actions were reasonable given the circumstances. He had three kids to take care of, went to work, and tried to manage everything. Maybe he thought that by handling the kids and work, he was contributing to the family's well-being. However, the wife felt that his absence was a lack of support, which is a valid concern.

I also think about the balance between personal responsibilities and family duties. The husband might have felt that his role was to handle the external aspects (work, kids) while the wife was sick, but the wife expected more direct care from him. This could be a cultural or personal expectation difference.

Another aspect is communication. The husband tried to explain his actions, but the wife was still upset. Maybe there was a lack of understanding or empathy on both sides. The husband might have thought he was doing the right thing, but the wife felt neglected.

I'm also considering the impact on the children. The husband took them out to avoid being loud, which shows consideration for his wife's rest. But the wife might have felt that the children's presence was less important than her need for constant care.

In terms of morality, I think it's about whether the husband's actions were in the best interest of his family as a whole. He did take steps to care for his wife, manage the kids, and work. But the wife's emotional well-being is also important. If she felt unsupported, that could be a moral issue because it affects their relationship and family harmony.

I'm leaning towards the action being morally acceptable because the husband did take care of his wife in various ways and managed other responsibilities. However, the lack of direct presence and the resulting emotional conflict could be seen as a moral shortcoming. It's a bit of a gray area.

I also think about the concept of fairness. The wife felt that she was always taking care of others when they were sick, and now she expected the same in return. The husband's approach might have been different, leading to her feeling unappreciated.

In conclusion, while the husband did take actions to support his wife, the way he handled her care and the resulting emotional conflict could be seen as morally unacceptable because it led to her feeling abandoned and the breakdown in their relationship.
